bug_semantics: RabbitConnectionFactoryBean.setUri() immediately delegated an amqps URI to the RabbitMQ client while the bean's secure setUpSSL() path remained conditional on a separate useSSL flag. With the default false flag, the client created encrypted TLS using its permissive trust-everything setup, so neither the broker certificate nor hostname was verified and an active network attacker could impersonate the broker.
flaw_origin: Commit 3b605cddbfd502946e841ddecd304f0ca308710f added RabbitConnectionFactoryBean and first wrote both direct setUri delegations while also making secure SSL initialization depend on the independent useSSL boolean. Its immediate parent 64be3f1ba86561f5af53abb0f99be25a9bbd1d4c has no RabbitConnectionFactoryBean.java, establishing this as the smallest surviving project commit that introduced the flawed control flow; the commit says the class was ported from Spring XD but is not a squash aggregate and exposes no finer member history in this repository.
ai_marker: absent: BIC author Gary Russell <grussell@gopivotal.com>, committer Artem Bilan <abilan@gopivotal.com>; the full commit object has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker
evidence: The published CVE.org record at https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-41714 states that setUri("amqps://...") without setUseSSL(true) yields TLS without certificate or hostname verification; it lists affected 4.0.0-4.0.3, 3.2.0-3.2.10, 3.1.0-3.1.15, and 2.4.0-2.4.17 ranges and remains PUBLISHED.

The first-party advisory https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-41714 identifies TrustEverythingTrustManager as the bypass sink and lists OSS fixes 4.0.4 and 3.2.11; the assigned GHSA bundle has withdrawn_at=null and the same affected ranges.

git show 3b605cddbfd502946e841ddecd304f0ca308710f:spring-rabbit/src/main/java/org/springframework/amqp/rabbit/connection/RabbitConnectionFactoryBean.java shows lines 133-145 directly calling connectionFactory.setUri() and lines 57-68 defining a default-false useSSL flag; git log --all --reverse -S'public void setUri(URI uri)' identifies this commit as the first writer.

git show 64be3f1ba86561f5af53abb0f99be25a9bbd1d4c:spring-rabbit/src/main/java/org/springframework/amqp/rabbit/connection/RabbitConnectionFactoryBean.java fails because the path does not exist, directly verifying parent-tree absence.
git show v4.0.3:.../RabbitConnectionFactoryBean.java shows setUri() still directly delegates at lines 488-507 while createInstance() calls setUpSSL() only when useSSL is true at lines 775-780.

Direct fix 0373cde52a9934d476079bceda445d948b70f112 stores the URI, detects the amqps scheme before SSL setup, invokes setUpSSL(), and only then applies the URI; its parent is 1e5df361f74fd82180810503260b9b8114eed985 and v4.0.4 contains the fix while v4.0.3 does not.

Patch-equivalent backport 690da5c2e614298728a955f52c75039969a6c3c7 is contained in v3.2.11 and absent from v3.2.10; both backports name original direct-fix commit 3a38397bd3fc89c452ab05086b9fb1e8f7769d24 in their commit objects.

git merge-base --is-ancestor verifies the BIC is contained in v2.4.0, v3.1.0, v3.2.0, and v4.0.0, preceding every vendor-listed affected line; the assigned GHSA provides no OSS first_patched_version for the 3.1 and 2.4 lines.
git show -s --format=fuller plus the complete BIC message confirms human author/committer identities and no AI, co-author, generated-with, or bot trailer on the BIC.
reasoning: The advisory's source-to-sink path matches the repository: the bean's URI setter configured the underlying client immediately, whereas certificate-validating SSL setup occurred later only under the independently configured useSSL flag. The class-creation commit is the first repository object containing both sides of that mismatch, and its direct parent lacks the entire file; later exception-wrapping edits preserve rather than originate the mechanism. The 4.0 direct fix and its 3.2 backport reorder configuration so amqps selects secure SSL before the client receives the URI, and their containment begins at the published patched tags. Because the atomic BIC's commit object names human author and committer identities and contains no AI marker, the real vulnerability is NOT_AI.
